commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): a Multiplayer page with the lobby and the server connection, version 0.1.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A new native mod, the first step of online play: the menu, the lobby
and the connection, with nothing of the game played together yet.

- A Multiplayer entry in the front end's Options list (mod interface
  1.5's menu pages), whose page shows the launcher's Multiplayer name
  (OPENRAC_PLAYER_NAME) and three actions: Find match (any open party
  with room, or a new open one), Create match (a private party) and
  Join by code (six characters entered with the pad). Then the lobby:
  the code, the…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): Multiplayer in the main menu under Load Game, its pages the game's own menus, version 0.2.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The mod moves to interface 1.7: the title's main menu reads New Game,
Load Game, Multiplayer, Options, and its pages are drawn by the game's
front end (its frames, list, font, prompt box and sounds) instead of a
page of rectangles and text in Options:

- Home: Find match, Create match, Join by code (each waits for the
  server's hello), and the player's name.
- Join by code: a row per character, stepped with Left and Right through
  the code alphabet, then Join; the lobby takes its place once…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): Direct connect in the menu and a Name setting, version 0.3.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Home gets Direct connect, a second-level page with Host directly and Join by
address. Hosting listens on 7770 (TCP and UDP) and opens the lobby, whose title
shows the LAN addresses with the port; a taken port stays on the page with the
reason in the footer; Leave asks "Stop hosting?". Join by address steps the four
octets and the port with Left and Right on 64-choice ring rows (held, they go
ten at a time) and keeps the last address for the game. Leaving a direct party
returns to Home and to…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): party descriptions and the party list in the protocol
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
CREATE carries the party's description (the host's save in words),
INFO carries it back, and LIST (opcode 8) asks for the parties with
room, as the server now answers. The session keeps the description
and the last list; the embedded host of Direct connect answers LIST
with its one party and keeps a description as the server does
(printable ASCII, trimmed, 48 characters). The lobby's start notice
loses its "not playable yet".

Tests: CREATE, LIST and INFO byte for byte, an older server's…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): play the host's game together and show the other players
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
coop.hpp runs the game side of a party on the SDK's play calls, a tick
at a time: the host's Start sends PLAY (a new game, or its save in
16,000-byte pieces) and starts its own game; a member starts the same
from the title without touching its card. The host says its level once
a second (LEVEL) and members in another level travel there; a member
who joins late gets the host's progress as it is (save_capture), and
one back in the title asks again (WANT).

Every game sends its Ratchet 20 times a…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): Browse games, a save picker and Start that plays, version 0.4.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Home's Find match becomes Browse games: a page listing the games
others host (their host, save and players), refreshed every 3 seconds,
with Refresh at the top and a line pointing at Create match when there
are none. Create match and Host directly first open Choose a save: New
game and the memory card's saves with their planet, gold bolts and
time. The lobby shows what the party plays, and Start now starts it
for everyone; a member back in the title gets Join the game. The Home
cursor moves up…

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): build on Windows, where Winsock's min and max macros broke std::min
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The library and its test define NOMINMAX on Windows, so host.cpp's
std::min compiles again (MSVC read the windows.h macro).

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the host's world shared with the party
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
world.hpp runs the shared world on interface 1.9's world calls. The
host's game runs the level; each member in its level drives every
placed moby that has an update of its own and poses it from the host's
WORLD snapshots (the 48 mobys nearest that member that moved, 15 times
a second, as state) through a buffer per moby. Placed mobys gone in
the host's game are gone in everyone's (KILLED, and ALIVE for one that
arrives later); creatures and bolts the host's game makes are made
there too (SPAWN,…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): refuse another build, leave a party's end for the title, version 0.5.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
PLAY carries the host's build (the mod's version, OpenRAC's, the
disc): a member with another refuses the game ("Incompatible version")
and does not ask again. A member playing the host's game when the
party ends (the host left, the connection went) goes back to the
title, whose lobby says why. The mod needs interface 1.9 now (the top
CMakeLists.txt builds it with an SDK of 1.9 or newer). README: the
shared world, its DATA kinds, the limits; the manifest's description.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a menu never empties the world; deaths only from the game's word
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Pausing in one game deleted mobys in the other's: the pause menu brings
up mobys of its own, so a game in it listed none of the level's, and the
world took every one it no longer saw for dead (the host sent KILLED
for all of them, a member BROKE for every crate). A death is now known
only from the game listing a placed moby dead (interface 1.9's
OPENRAC_MOBY_DEAD), and a tick the game lists nothing changes nothing.
A member arriving in the host's level gets the host's dead mobys (DEAD,
in place…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): scenes end together, version 0.6.0
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The host's skip counts: when the host is out of its scene (skipped or
played out) for a second, a member still in one is skipped through the
game's own skip (play_skip); a member's Start does nothing while the
host's scene plays. Nobody gets control back until everyone is out: the
host waits for its members (at most 10 seconds), a member for the
host's scene. LEVEL carries the host's scene, POSE whether its sender
plays one. README: menus, scenes, the classes, the limits.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): say in the log when scenes start, are skipped and end
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A scene's start (host or member, the host's too), a member's Start held
for the host, a skip asked for the party, its end (after the party's
skip or not), and the barrier's wait and release are lines in the log,
so a test run shows what scenes did. Tests: the scene test checks the
lines.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a skip in any game skips the scene or movie in every game
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The user's test: the host skipped the intro movies and its scenes, and
the member, whose movies only Start ends, never left the first: the
host never had a member in its level (no snapshots), and the member
logged no scene. Movies were not shared at all, and in a scene only the
host's skip counted.

Now Start pressed in a scene or a movie, in any game of the party, is
a SKIP (kind 18): a member's goes to the host, which skips its own and
passes it on to everyone. A game in a scene skips it…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the world log counts live and driven mobys every 5 s
commits.author: Veradictus

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the others' Ratchets hold their wrench and weapons and fire their shots
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A pose now carries what its Ratchet wears and holds (after its 65 bytes,
so an older mod's pose still reads, wearing nothing), passed to the
figure each tick; a SHOT (kind 19) carries each Blaster shot and bomb,
fired by the figure as far behind as its poses play, in its level only.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a figure's animation runs on between two poses, a stop is not overshot
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The animation came from the nearer of the two poses around the playback
cursor, so the key shown jumped three keys at a time in a run and waited in
between. Within one seq the place in it now runs on from the one pose's to
the other's (key and time, and the speed); a new seq still comes from the
nearer one. Past the newest pose the figure no longer carries on along the
velocity of a sender that was slowing down (a stop), and a sender back after
a second of silence with its count started again…

commits.headline: test(multiplayer): a pause in either game keeps the world whole on the other side
commits.author: Veradictus

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the party flies with the host's ship and arrives together
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Only the host flies the ship while a party plays: a member's planet select to another planet
lands the ship again where it is (the Ship_TravelTo hook, rac1.ship.travel_to), with a line over
the game saying why. When the host's ship leaves for another planet, LEVEL carries the travel (a
count, the planet, whether the party still arrives) at once, and each member leaves its level
that moment from wherever it is (playing, a scene, the pause menu, a vendor), asked again until a
load says it went.…

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): leaving a party goes back to the title's Multiplayer page
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The player whose party goes while it plays (Leave party, the host ending the
party, a lost connection) leaves its level at once, from playing, a scene or
the pause menu, and the title opens the Multiplayer page, saying why when the
player did not leave by itself. The host leaving now takes its own game back
too instead of keeping it alone in an emptied level; a member leaving goes
alone and the party plays on.

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the host's in-level scenes play in every game of the party
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A scene of the level's own (a person spoken to, a place reached, Veldin's opening) is started by
a moby's update, and the members' copies of those mobys are driven from the host's, so the scene
played in the host's game alone: at Veldin's start only the host saw the opening, and the six
actors it made never reached the members.

The host now tells each scene it starts (SCENE: the level's number of it, a sequence, the ms it
has played; again once a second while it plays, and at its end), and a…

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): a skip ends only the scene it was pressed in
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A party's skip was kept for 1.5 s and applied to whatever scene played
then, so the skip of a movie or of the host's previous scene cut off the
member's copy of the host's next scene right after it started.

Every scene of the host's is now an instance (SCENE's sequence). SKIP
says what it was pressed in (the host's scene by its sequence, a game's
own scene, a movie) and each game skips only that one, while it plays: a
skip of an earlier scene, of another play, or without the ids (an…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): the host's hidden mobys hidden in members' games, and a despawn log
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A placed moby's own update hides and shows it (an enemy waiting to appear), and
a member's game no longer runs the update of one it drives, so its copy kept
the hidden state of the moment the drive began. WORLD now carries the host's
hidden flag (25 bytes an entry, 46 entries a datagram) and the member hides or
shows its driven copy so; a moby the host stops sending is held as it is.

The despawn_log setting (off by default) writes a despawn: line for each moby
that leaves the level, or is…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): a verbose log of the party's world, for the pause despawns
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The verbose_log setting (or OPENRAC_MP_TRACE=1) writes an [mp-trace] line for
each event into mp-trace.log in the game's working directory, beside its
run.log, which says where once. Each line names the frame, the time, the side
(host, member, solo) and what happened: the pauses (phase, the level's game
mode, a menu entered and left, and each menu tick the camera mods read, the
camera the game's run list measured from and the level's camera the pause
menu puts up, from the port's moby_run), the…

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): say why a player's figure is no longer shown
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A figure removed left no line in the log: a member closing its game while
the host paused read as the pause despawning it. drop_figure now logs the
player and the reason (out of the party, silent, in another level, ...).

Adds a test replaying the report: the host's pause menu up for 4.4 s keeps
the member's figure, which goes only when the member leaves.

commits.headline: fix(multiplayer): Start waits for every member's Ready
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The lobby carried Ready from member to host, but nothing read it: the
host's Start went through whoever was ready. Start is now dim (the port
plays the refusal) until every member but the host is ready, and the
session and the co-op refuse it too. A member who joins is not ready,
so it takes all-ready away until it says so. The member list marks each
member ready or not ready, and the host's count line says when not all
are. The embedded Direct host carries the same lobby, so it does the
same.

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): hide the other players' figures while a scene plays
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A scene in this game hides the other players' Ratchets (moby_hide on the figure's slot) and
their pieces (held as hidden) instead of removing them, drops their shots, and shows them again
once the scene is over. A game that cannot hide a figure takes it out for the scene.

commits.headline: feat(multiplayer): only the host skips scenes and movies
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A member's Start in a scene or a movie is taken out of its pad and skips nothing anywhere; the
banner says "Only the host can skip" for 3 s. The host's skip still skips everywhere by the
per-scene SKIP ids, and a member's SKIP (an older build's) the host ignores and logs. The
README's rules say so, and that scenes hide the other players.
